signature_moves: The icon IS the gesture: the glyph is the space symbol / spacebar keycap, and Quick Look is invoked by pressing spacebar — the icon depicts the trained action, not the app (Jakob's Law as brand)
Monochrome discipline: zero hue anywhere; near-black stage + metallic-white glyph differentiate by subtraction in a Dock of saturated squircles
Demonstrative backdrop: ~100+ real file extensions shown as a constellation instead of a 'supports many formats' claim (proof by display)

aesthetic.direction: Industrial/utilitarian minimal on an Apple hero stage: dark near-black ground, a single metallic system-glyph, system type — no accent, no illustration

psychology: Jakob's Law — icon reuses the trained spacebar->Quick Look mental model; the mark predicts its own gesture
Von Restorff effect — a single grayscale mark reads as 'the different one' against saturated Dock neighbours; high pop at 16-32px
Aesthetic-Usability / first impression — the centered dark hero is a ~50ms thesis (premium, format-agnostic) via the extension galaxy
Description-experience gap — showing real file extensions demonstrates breadth rather than asserting it
notes: CRITICAL for synthesis: no app UI surface was provided. gallery is empty; the only files are a marketing cover.png (composite) and a 256px icon.png. The cover contains NO app window/chrome/controls, so lineage (unknown/low) and era (unknown) cannot be UI-evidenced and nothing here may feed macOS UI canon or a UI cluster. This was Workflow-A-scoped, so the icon was captured as brand evidence only, NOT run through the full 12-point icon rubric (Workflow B) — a dedicated icon digest would promote icon/* readings.
